rows.episode_title: Not So Bad Wolf / Chicken of the Sea
rows.synopsis: Piper tries to save the Three Little Pigs from the Big Bad Wolf. When Terry Turtle hatches all alone, Piper and Papa help him find his way.
rows.situation: Benjamin's Captain Spin crash lands into Piper's book castle, and the apology does not rebuild it: she bans him from her room. Story time picks up the wreckage, because the Big Bad Wolf is about to blow down a pig house, and Piper interrupts to ask him nicely to stop.
rows.coping: Papa teaches the actual lever: character is not what you like, it is how you treat others. Rewrites that only change the wolf's hobbies just move the mess around, until Piper writes kindness in, and the frame story repairs itself when Captain Spin returns, changed, to help rebuild.
rows.notes: mixed age: fairy-tale slapstick plays 2-4 but the double lesson, banning a sibling versus rewriting a character, plays 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Piper tries to save the Three Little Pigs' omits the frame-story fight with Benjamin that the wolf tale is quietly solving. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: When Benjamin's spinning crashes Piper's book castle, her room closes to him, and bedtime story time becomes the negotiation table. Piper interrupts the Three Little Pigs to reform the Big Bad Wolf, and learns that swapping pizza for tuba for ballet only relocates the wreckage: character is how you treat others. Her final draft writes a helping wolf, and Captain Spin, take notes, comes back to help rebuild the castle he flattened.

rows.episode_title: Not So Bad Wolf / Chicken of the Sea
rows.synopsis: Piper tries to save the Three Little Pigs from the Big Bad Wolf. When Terry Turtle hatches all alone, Piper and Papa help him find his way.
rows.situation: Terry Turtle hatches alone with one job, follow the moon to the ocean, and the beach supplies driftwood, dunes, and pirate crabs between him and it. Duckston keeps writing gave-up-and-ate-oatmeal endings, because the space between the puzzle bins has taught him lost things stay lost.
rows.coping: Piper keeps rewriting past every impossible, seaweed slingshot, coconut-shell glider, a lullaby played to pirates, and the story ends at Turtle Island with family. Back in the classroom, the impossible sticker is sitting exactly where creative thinking put it.
rows.notes: mixed age: pirate crabs play 2-4; the tug-of-war between a friend who says impossible and a story that keeps going, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Piper and Papa help him find his way' omits Duckston's surrender endings, the crew's escape-by-lullaby, and the sticker echo that closes the loop. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Terry Turtle hatches alone on a beach, and every step toward the ocean grows an obstacle, driftwood, dunes, a one-way pirate crew. Duckston keeps writing endings where everyone gives up and eats oatmeal, and Piper keeps interrupting with creative ideas until the story delivers Terry to his family. Back in class, the sticker that fell into the forever-lost space turns out not to be lost after all.

rows.episode_title: The Elephant of Surprise / The Chicken and the Egg
rows.synopsis: Piper and the Three Billy Goats Gruff outsmart the Bridge Troll. The King's Knights help Piper solve a royal mystery.
rows.situation: Piper jumps into the Billy Goats Gruff and helpfully tells the troll the goats' whole plan, which ends the story on the spot. Mrs. Slothworth's lesson, every story has the element of surprise, gets taken literally, an elephant of surprise, and the rewrite has to win the meadow back with tricks the troll cannot predict.
rows.coping: Piper's second draft gives the troll nothing to expect: a fake long-way-around, coconut rattle, goats that faint, and a brand-new bridge built while he argues with a tummy growl. The troll hates surprises, which is exactly the point, and Theodore's magic trick closes the loop.
rows.notes: mixed age: fainting goats play 2-4; hearing that helping can spoil a story, and fixing the fix, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'outsmart the Bridge Troll' omits that Piper's first intervention is the problem and the elephant pun drives the whole structure. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Piper's helpful interruption tells the troll the goats' entire plan and ends the story early, her first rewrite that backfired. Papa introduces the element of surprise, via a literal elephant in Rapunzel's tower, and the rerun of the Billy Goats Gruff becomes a masterclass in misdirection, complete with fainted goats and a secretly built second bridge. The troll surrenders to a story he could not predict.

rows.episode_title: The Elephant of Surprise / The Chicken and the Egg
rows.synopsis: Piper and the Three Billy Goats Gruff outsmart the Bridge Troll. The King's Knights help Piper solve a royal mystery.
rows.situation: Piper's art project has become a paint-glitter-paper avalanche, and the harder she grabs, the worse it gets. Story time hands her Humpty Dumpty in pieces and a rhyme that says nobody could put him together again, with a king's glue locked behind an obstacle course of doom.
rows.coping: Papa offers the writer's tool, a story beat, one small thing that moves the story forward, and Piper stacks them: a snack break, a map, a quest, one more beat after every failure. Humpty gets glued, whole again, and the same beats un-do the art avalanche at home.
rows.notes: mixed age: the sandwich knight plays 2-4; a big overwhelming mess broken into next steps, in craft and in story, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'The King's Knights help Piper solve a royal mystery' is the other story; tags anchor on segment_title plus the script. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Piper's cleanup attempt is losing to her own art supplies, and Humpty Dumpty is losing to gravity, with a rhyme insisting he stays broken. Papa teaches story beats, one small step that moves things forward, and Piper beats her way through sandwiches, maps, quests, and an obstacle course of doom to the king's glue. Humpty ends up whole, and the same method tidies the bedroom that started it all.

rows.episode_title: Hercul-easy / The Lion, the Mouse and the Chicken
rows.synopsis: In Greece, Piper attempts to make Hercules' heroic journey easier. A lion with a thorn in his paw resists help.
rows.situation: Piper interrupts Hercules' trials and clears every obstacle, boulder moved, wall scaled, maze opened, so the hero-in-training can just walk to his trophy. The urn story stops: no trophy, because nothing was in his way.
rows.coping: Papa names the missing piece, an obstacle, and Piper's next rewrite puts all the obstacles back, boulder, wall, runaway boulder, broken wheel. Hercules earns two trophies, and the classroom hoop gets raised on purpose, because easy was boring.
rows.notes: mixed age: the chariot chase plays 2-4; the idea that difficulty is not the enemy of the thing you want but the price of it, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'make Hercules' heroic journey easier' omits that the easy version fails, the obstacles get restored on purpose, and the Parthenon gets saved instead. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Piper does young Hercules the kindest possible sabotage, removing every obstacle between him and the hero's trophy, and the story refuses to end well. Papa explains that heroes are made by obstacles, not despite them, so the rewrite puts the boulder back, and a runaway boulder turns restoration into real heroics. Back at school, the basketball hoop goes back up: the game needs things in the way.

rows.episode_title: Hercul-easy / The Lion, the Mouse and the Chicken
rows.segment_title: The Lion, the Mouse and the Chicken
rows.synopsis: In Greece, Piper attempts to make Hercules' heroic journey easier. A lion with a thorn in his paw resists help.
rows.situation: Piper is at the doctor's office trying to rename herself out of a wing appointment, and the story supplies a lion with a thorn in his paw who refuses the mouse's help. Every game the lion tries with friends fails on the paw, and the thorn gets worse.
rows.coping: Piper's rewrite lets the lion be scared out loud and still say yes: might it hurt, yes a little, and we will count to three together. The thorn comes out, the games come back, and Piper walks into her own appointment asking Papa to count with her.
rows.notes: mixed age: patty-cake with a limp plays 2-4; fear of a short hurt versus a long one, and letting someone help, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'a lion with a thorn in his paw resists help' omits that the whole segment is Piper's own doctor fear wearing a lion costume. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Piper is hiding from a doctor's appointment under three fake names when Papa reads The Lion and the Mouse, whose hero refuses the one thing that would fix him. The lion's games evaporate and his paw gets worse, and Piper's rewrite gives him permission to be scared and counted through it. The moral arrives on time: let someone help you, even if you are scared, and the sprained wing gets wrapped in three counts flat.

rows.episode_title: Where's the Party? / Chicken Out West
rows.synopsis: Piper, Aladdin, and Genie search for the perfect place to host an ice cream party. Piper joins the Pony Express.
rows.situation: Piper interrupts Aladdin to spend a wish on the genie, who has granted everyone else's wishes and never had his own. The ice cream party keeps failing by location, desert heat, South Pole freeze, forest ants, even the moon, and the search for the perfect place starts burning the day.
rows.coping: The search ends by looking at what was already loved: the genie's own lamp, perfect temperature, zero ants, ping-pong included. Piper apologizes for the failed hunt, the party happens at home base, and the backyard kites find the same answer at the lake.
rows.notes: mixed age: the location-hopping gags play 2-4; the person who gives and gives getting a turn, and perfect being closer than far away, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'search for the perfect place' omits that the wish is for the genie, and that every exotic setting fails until the lamp wins. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Piper interrupts Aladdin mid-wish to ask a better question, when does the genie get a wish, and his ice cream party becomes the plot. Desert, South Pole, forest, and moon each ruin the party in a new way, until the perfect setting turns out to be the lamp the genie never wanted to leave. The grateful wish lands, and the backyard kite problem solves itself the same way, by changing where, not what.

rows.episode_title: Where's the Party? / Chicken Out West
rows.synopsis: Piper, Aladdin, and Genie search for the perfect place to host an ice cream party. Piper joins the Pony Express.
rows.situation: Miss Clara leaves the Penelope Pony story on a cliffhanger, mid-mountain, letter undelivered, and Piper has to wait a whole day. Writing the continuation means committing to what happens next, over a bear, a broken bridge, a runaway letter, and a final cliff of her own invention.
rows.coping: When Piper's own story reaches a cliff she cannot write past, Papa's questions, did they ask for help, did they build something, unstick the pen. The lasso climb delivers the birthday letter, and Duckston's top secret package keeps its own cliffhanger for the fun of it.
rows.notes: mixed age: the pony express romp plays 2-4; living inside suspense on purpose, and writing past the moment you do not know, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Piper joins the Pony Express' omits the cliffhanger lesson, the waiting-for-tomorrow stake, and that Piper's stuck moment mirrors Penelope's mountain. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Miss Clara's Pony Express story stops exactly where it gets dangerous, and Piper has to survive the suspense overnight. She writes Penelope's rescue herself, skis, bear, lasso, and discovers writers hit cliffs too, until the right question turns the blank page into a climb. The letter arrives for the birthday sister, and Duckston's mystery package holds its suspense like a professional.

rows.episode_title: Disco Chickens / Little Red and the Little Red Chicken
rows.synopsis: At a disco roller rink, Piper investigates how Grandma and Grandpa met. Piper tries to warn Little Red Riding Hood about the wolf.
rows.situation: Grandma and Grandpa each tell the story of the night they met, and the two versions contradict on the moose, the polar bear, and who was the best skater. Both insist theirs is one hundred percent right, and a first meeting has become an argument.
rows.coping: Piper's detective story refuses to pick a winner: she collects every point of view, DJ included, and writes one combined story where both chickens are right. The balloon explains the polar bear, the bump explains the meet-cute, and Benjamin's four-headed monster turns out to be golf clubs once he looks closer.
rows.notes: mixed age: the disco gags play 2-4; two people remembering the same event differently, and both being true, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Piper investigates how Grandma and Grandpa met' omits the contradictory-testimony structure and Benjamin's monster subplot that rhymes with it. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Grandma and Grandpa remember meeting at the disco roller rink, and their memories disagree, best skater, headstand moose, spinning polar bear. Piper writes a detective story that interviews the whole rink and discovers the fix is not picking a winner but weaving every point of view into one story. Benjamin, meanwhile, meets the basement's four-headed monster and finds golf clubs, both mysteries solved by a change of view.

rows.episode_title: Disco Chickens / Little Red and the Little Red Chicken
rows.segment_title: Little Red and the Little Red Chicken
rows.synopsis: At a disco roller rink, Piper investigates how Grandma and Grandpa met. Piper tries to warn Little Red Riding Hood about the wolf.
rows.situation: Theodore forgot the photo of the flower he grew for show-and-tell, and every crayon fails to match Zinnie's exact purple, so he wants to quit. In the story, Piper cannot finish her warning because there is nothing to compare the wolf to, as bad as a what.
rows.coping: Mrs. Slothworth hands them the missing tool, the simile, and it does double duty: Little Red gets her warning in time, grandma returns from go-karting in Bolivia to evict the house-sitting wolf, and Theodore finds Zinnie's purple in grape jelly. Describing the thing unlocks both stories.
rows.notes: mixed age: the freezing-out-the-wolf plays 2-4; vocabulary as rescue equipment, when you cannot say what you mean, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Piper tries to warn Little Red Riding Hood' omits the stuck-in-the-middle-of-a-simile beat and the classroom mirror in Theodore's purple problem. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Piper's warning to Little Red Riding Hood keeps collapsing at the same word: the wolf is as bad as a what. Meanwhile Theodore cannot show-and-tell the flower he grew because no crayon matches Zinnie's purple. One lesson, the simile, saves both stories, complete with a South-Pole-cold elephant, a house-sitting wolf, and grape jelly.

rows.episode_title: Dawn of Wonder Chicken / The Chicken Who Cried Wolf
rows.synopsis: Piper transforms into Wonder Chicken to save Chickenopolis. After a shepherd boy cries wolf, Piper asks him about his motivation.
rows.situation: The board game stalls without its Mer-Rooster piece, and Piper's homemade Wonder Chicken story stalls for the same reason in reverse: a hero with no past. Every villain trap defeats her, quack-tanium lasers, darkened labs, headphone monsters, because nothing in her history gives her a tool for any of it.
rows.coping: Grandma teaches the fix, a backstory, everything from a character's past that makes them who they are. A lightning-struck weather book, computer practice, a pet monster, and a boyhood friend named Quackles turn out to be the whole solution, and even the villain gets grounded by his mom.
rows.notes: mixed age: the potato slapstick plays 2-4; the writing lesson that a character's past explains her powers, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Piper transforms into Wonder Chicken' omits that the episode is a writing workshop in disguise, and that the villain's defeat is a revelation, not a fight. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Wonder Chicken faces a quack-tanium laser grid with no tools, because Piper wrote her a hero with no history. Grandma supplies the writer's term, backstory, and each new memory, a thunder-cluck book, library computer skills, a pet monster, a childhood friend, becomes a way through. Dr. Von Duck falls not to a punch but to being recognized, and a missing Mer-Rooster gets a backstory that beats the real toy.

rows.episode_title: Dawn of Wonder Chicken / The Chicken Who Cried Wolf
rows.synopsis: Piper transforms into Wonder Chicken to save Chickenopolis. After a shepherd boy cries wolf, Piper asks him about his motivation.
rows.situation: Theodore fakes injuries, twice, and nobody believes him, right before story time casts a boy who cries wolf twice and loses his sheep. Piper interviews her way to the motivations under both tricks: the boy wanted an audience that really listened, and the wolf wanted company on his birthday.
rows.coping: The rewrite swaps punishment for understanding: the boy gets his audience, the wolf gets a sheep-over party with the whole village, and afterward Theodore tells the truth himself, he was hurting in here, and needed some extra attention. He gets the hug, not a lecture.
rows.notes: mixed age: the party reveal plays 2-4; attention-seeking as a feeling with a reason, said out loud and met with a hug, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'a shepherd boy cries wolf' omits the motivation interviews, the wolf's lonely birthday, and Theodore's real confession afterward. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Theodore's fake injuries are followed by a story about a boy whose false wolf calls cost him his sheep, and Piper rewrites for motive instead of punishment: the boy wanted listeners, and the wolf stole sheep to fill a lonely birthday. The village ends up at a party, the boy sings for a real audience, and Theodore, having watched the whole thing, tells his own truth and gets a hug for it.

rows.episode_title: Arizona Chickenstone and the Temple of the Troll / The Chicken and the Beanstalk
rows.segment_title: Arizona Chickenstone and the Temple of the Troll
rows.synopsis: As a world explorer, Piper rescues an artifact from a hidden jungle temple. Piper reimagines Jack and the Beanstalk from the giant's perspective.
rows.situation: Theodore's journal says to take the path with the tree and the big rock, but every path has both, and the creek is lost until details return. In the story, Piper's adventure starts as a list of trusty gear and no pictures, quicksand included.
rows.coping: Papa's writing tool is vivid detail, enough description to picture it, and each dose does real work: troll footprints pick the path, vines escape the quicksand, a different brick opens a secret passage, stalactites hold the rope. Back on the trail, a big round green rock with moss finds the creek.
rows.notes: mixed age: the giant orange of doom plays 2-4; description as a survival tool for stories and for trails, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'rescues an artifact from a hidden jungle temple' omits the lost-creek frame and that every escape is powered by a writing lesson. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Theodore's explorer journal points to a tree and a big rock, which describes every path in the woods, so Papa reads an explorer story where vivid detail saves the day. Piper writes Arizona Chickenstone through quicksand, troll traps, and a collapsing temple using nothing but well-chosen specifics, then borrows the technique to find a mossy rock. The creek appears, exactly where the details said.

rows.episode_title: Arizona Chickenstone and the Temple of the Troll / The Chicken and the Beanstalk
rows.synopsis: As a world explorer, Piper rescues an artifact from a hidden jungle temple. Piper reimagines Jack and the Beanstalk from the giant's perspective.
rows.situation: Benjamin's gloppy paint project looks like a mess, and Jack's harp theft looks like a happy ending, until Piper asks the second question. From the giant's side, the beanstalk brought a ghost, a theft, and a stolen practice partner with a library show coming up.
rows.coping: Piper writes the story again from the giant's eyes, Jack hears what the harp really meant and returns it with an apology, and everyone's ending gets rewritten together, music in the woods, weekly. Then Mom asks Benjamin's perspective, and the gloppy paint becomes a gift Emilo can feel.
rows.notes: mixed age: the giant's haunted-house comedy plays 2-4; perspective-taking as a habit, with a blind friend who experiences art by touch, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'reimagines Jack and the Beanstalk from the giant's perspective' omits Emilo, the frame-story apology, and the shared ending. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Jack's beanstalk caper ends happily for Jack, and Piper notices someone did not get a happy ending: the giant whose harp disappeared. Rewriting the story from her point of view turns a victory into an apology, and a new ending where the music belongs to everyone, including Jack's mom. Mom applies the same lesson at home and learns Benjamin's gloppy mess is a painting made to be touched.

rows.episode_title: Dr. Chickenstein / The Sorcerer's Thesaurus
rows.synopsis: On Halloween, Piper writes a spooky monster story. Piper helps the Sorcerer's Apprentice outsmart a four-headed dragon.
rows.situation: Duckston's moon costume piece is missing, Benjamin refuses his own costume because it is not spooky enough, and Piper's Halloween story has a monster that will not scare anyone: she wrote spooky and described nothing.
rows.coping: Papa coaches Piper through the five senses, and the monster gets a look, a growl, slimy claws, and old-wet-laundry smell until the room is properly spooked. The same tool finds the moon, round, white, string attached, squishy, light as air, a balloon, up.
rows.notes: mixed age: the spook-level gags play 2-4; saying spooky is not showing spooky, and senses as search equipment, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Piper writes a spooky monster story' omits the five-sense rewrite, the missing balloon moon, and Benjamin's costume rescue. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Piper's Halloween monster is a failure by the villagers' reviews, because she wrote the word spooky instead of building one. Sense by sense, Papa's story-time workshop makes it real, and the same describing trick solves Duckston's missing moon, which turns out to be a balloon floating overhead. Trick-or-treating finally launches, costumes complete.

rows.episode_title: Dr. Chickenstein / The Sorcerer's Thesaurus
rows.synopsis: On Halloween, Piper writes a spooky monster story. Piper helps the Sorcerer's Apprentice outsmart a four-headed dragon.
rows.situation: The apprentice tries one spell to clean up, breaks the cleanup, and breaks it again, then learns the staff's rule the hard way: the same magic word cannot be used twice in one day. Fast is spent, big is spent, and four dragon heads are guarding the slippers.
rows.coping: Piper supplies the loophole, a synonym, another word that means the same thing, and the apprentice runs the ladder: swift, leap, immense, then kind, friendly, and pleasant, one per head. The slippers go home, the dragon gets warm socks, and the sorcerer hands over a promotion.
rows.notes: mixed age: the four-headed politeness offensive plays 2-4; running out of words for what you need, and growing your vocabulary instead, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'helps the Sorcerer's Apprentice outsmart a four-headed dragon' omits the magic-word rule and that synonyms are the weapon. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: A sorcerer's apprentice with one magic word per day is in trouble, because he already said fast and big. Piper interrupts with the fix: synonyms, swift and leap and immense, then a different nice-adjacent word for each of four dragon heads. The slippers come home carried by newly polite dragons, and the apprentice earns a thesaurus of his own.

rows.episode_title: A Chicken Carol
rows.synopsis: When Ebenezer Wolf decides to cancel the holidays, Piper teams up with the Three Little Pigs to save the season. The chicken family throws a holiday party.
rows.situation: Ebenezer Wolf cancels every holiday at once and confiscates the presents, decorations, and eggnog, because he only ever gets socks and only sees fuss. Tiny Pig keeps making his yearly snowflake for the wolf anyway, the one delivery the wolf never lets him make.
rows.coping: Piper picks the theme before the plot, giving, and writes three ghosts of giving, past, present, and future, to show the wolf what he already knows: the one time he gave mittens away, it felt great. He uncancels the holidays, gives Tiny Pig scissors and paper, and receives the best snowflake of his life.
rows.notes: special episode: holiday special with the whole class party frame. mixed age: the ghost gags play 2-4; the mechanics of a change of heart, theme first, ghosts as evidence, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'teams up with the Three Little Pigs to save the season' omits the ghost structure, Tiny Pig's snowflake thread, and the kids' own written gifts at the party. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Ebenezer Wolf cancels the entire holiday season and confiscates the town's joy, and Piper's rewrite gives him the traditional three ghosts with a theme attached: giving. Past reminds him how good generosity felt, present shows him Tiny Pig's undeliverable snowflake, and future shows a town celebrating anyway. The wolf uncancels everything, the party gifts become written ones, and Tiny Pig's snowflake finally lands.

rows.episode_title: Captain Claw's Clawsome Quest / Cinderella's Story
rows.synopsis: Piper sets sail with a pirate crew to search for treasure. When a favorite book falls apart, Piper and friends put it back in sequence.
rows.situation: CJ is too fast for anyone to want to race her, and Captain Claw is too good for anyone to want to compete, so the greatest pirate on the seven seas quits for pancakes. Piper writes her a foil, Captain Glitterbeard, mean where she is kind, cowardly where she is brave.
rows.coping: The foil makes the quest worth having: a treacherous purple pearl, a sea monster, a crew that works because their captain is kind. CJ gets a race back the same way, and runs her fastest time ever with someone actually beside her.
rows.notes: mixed age: pirate slapstick plays 2-4; being so good that nobody plays with you anymore, and competition as a gift, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'sets sail with a pirate crew to search for treasure' omits that the quest exists because someone wrote a rival, and the CJ frame. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Captain Claw retires undefeated into the pancake business because winning got boring, and CJ's running has the same problem, too fast to race. Piper writes Claw a foil, Glitterbeard, everything she is not, and the toughest treasure quest of her life makes pirating fun again. The frame resolves in sneakers: give the fastest kid a competitor, and everyone runs faster.

rows.episode_title: Captain Claw's Clawsome Quest / Cinderella's Story
rows.synopsis: Piper sets sail with a pirate crew to search for treasure. When a favorite book falls apart, Piper and friends put it back in sequence.
rows.situation: Cinderella's old book loses its pages mid-read, and the reassembled story makes no sense: ball before chores, carriage before magic. CJ's clapping game is falling apart the same way, hands that cannot find the sequence.
rows.coping: Mrs. Slothworth names the tool, sequence, the order things happen in, and the kids sort the pages, chores, magic, carriage, ball, until the story works. The missing ending gets written new, a fairy god-chicken teaches the Pumpkin Slide step by step, and the clapping game clicks.
rows.notes: mixed age: the Pumpkin Slide number plays 2-4; making sense of a story by ordering what happens first, next, and last, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'a favorite book falls apart' omits the out-of-order comedy, the written ending, and the clapping-game parallel. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Cinderella arrives at the ball twice, does chores after dancing, and rides a carriage that was never magicked, because the well-loved book dropped its pages and got reassembled wrong. The kids rebuild the sequence, invent an ending, and dance the Pumpkin Slide in the correct order at last. CJ's clapping game gets the same treatment, one step at a time.

rows.episode_title: Funky Chicken / Hansel & Gretel and the Chicken
rows.synopsis: Piper rewrites a time-honored tale to make it her own. Papa's friend shares his passion for hip-hop.
rows.situation: Papa's friend brings hip-hop to story time, and Piper meets a classic tale that is somebody else's rhythm: how do you rewrite a story that everyone already knows, so it is still the story and still yours.
rows.coping: The hip-hop frame shows the way, same story, new flow: beats for the huffing, rhymes for the huff-and-puff, and a fairy tale that finds its own groove. Piper's version keeps every story bone and changes every step.
rows.notes: vibe call: hip-hop episode, high energy; noted for calibration. mixed age: the beat-based retelling plays 2-4 as sound and motion; remixing something classic so it becomes yours, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Piper rewrites a time-honored tale to make it her own' omits the hip-hop frame entirely. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Papa's friend brings hip-hop to story time, and the lesson lands in the remix: a classic story can keep its bones and find a brand-new rhythm. Piper retells a time-honored tale in beats and rhymes, discovering that making a story your own is not replacing it, it is dancing with it.

rows.episode_title: Funky Chicken / Hansel & Gretel and the Chicken
rows.synopsis: Piper rewrites a time-honored tale to make it her own. Papa's friend shares his passion for hip-hop.
rows.situation: Piper's first Hansel and Gretel draft made Benjamin more scared, not less: spooky woods, a blamed brother, a witch loom. In the frame, Benjamin demands Piper's truck with a demand instead of an ask and gets a no that feels like the ending.
rows.coping: Papa names tone, what a writer does to create a feeling, and Piper tunes it piece by piece: a calm line for Gretel, cartwheels instead of walking, a witch whose scary party becomes a tea dance party. Benjamin tries the technique out loud on his sister, pretty please with strawberries on top, and the truck appears.
rows.notes: mixed age: the witch's glow-up plays 2-4; naming the tone of a story and of an ask, then adjusting both, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Piper rewrites a time-honored tale' omits the tone lesson, the scared frame, and the ask-differently resolution. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Hansel and Gretel comes back from the shelf scarier than Piper remembered, so she rewrites it live, changing the tone instead of the plot: calm words, cartwheels, and a witch who just needs guests for her tea party. The technique escapes the book when Benjamin asks for the purple truck with a completely different tone, and gets a yes.

rows.episode_title: Save the Stalk! / Why Did the Chicken Cross the Road?
rows.synopsis: Grandpa encourages Piper to help a struggling storybook character. A friendly lion looks to improve his comedy act.
rows.situation: The knights arrive to chop the beanstalk for a carriage parking lot, on royal orders, and the king has a garden's worth of reasons not to listen. Persuasion attempt one, ladybugs, bounces off, and the knights' lances are already out.
rows.coping: Papa teaches persuasive writing, a goal plus reasons that matter to the listener: ladybugs for the king's nature side, giant pinecones for his crafts side, mushrooms for the troll's stomach. Each audience gets its own reason, the decree flips, and at home the kids write their own persuasive case to stay up and smell the jasmine.
rows.notes: mixed age: the googly-eyed pinecone plays 2-4; changing a mind by arguing the other person's reasons instead of your own, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Grandpa encourages Piper to help a struggling storybook character' omits the three-audience persuasion ladder and the bedtime-frame payoff. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The king's knights are ordered to fell the beanstalk for a carriage lot, and Piper saves it with persuasive writing, goal first, then a reason shaped for each listener: ladybugs for the king, giant craft pinecones, mushrooms for a hungry bridge troll. Every persuasion lands except the one aimed at a cowless Mysterious Dude, who gives the last magic bean for free because the reasons were good. The kids then write their own persuasive case to stay up and smell the night-blooming jasmine, and win.

rows.episode_title: Save the Stalk! / Why Did the Chicken Cross the Road?
rows.segment_title: Why Did the Chicken Cross the Road?
rows.synopsis: Grandpa encourages Piper to help a struggling storybook character. A friendly lion looks to improve his comedy act.
rows.situation: Lion promised Mouse a comedy show for her birthday and has nothing: one joke, a tough-room porcupine review, and a clock running out. Piper's own punchline, why did the chicken cross the road, is waiting at the end of the story.
rows.coping: Grandpa and Piper build the show from types of comedy: jokes, physical comedy, and surprise comedy, taught by the Elephant of Surprise. The birthday show mixes all three, and the answer to the old joke turns out to be a story with a funny ending.
rows.notes: mixed age: the surprise-comedy payoff plays 2-4; stage fright met with a toolkit and practice, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'a friendly lion looks to improve his comedy act' omits the three comedy types, the porcupine's tough review, and the joke-as-story reveal. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Lion owes the birthday girl a comedy show and has one joke and no set, so Grandpa and Piper coach him through the types: knock-knock jokes, physical comedy, and surprise comedy from the Elephant of Surprise. A porcupine's tough-room review nearly sinks him, but the birthday performance lands, whisker wiggle included, and the chicken's road crossing gets its punchline at last.

rows.episode_title: Mary Had a Little Chicken / The Princess, the Chicken, and the Pea
rows.synopsis: Piper puts fun genre twists on a familiar favorite. When a royal athlete can't fall asleep, Piper hunts the cause.
rows.situation: Movie night dies in a neighborhood blackout, and a nursery rhyme is the only screen available. Piper retells Mary Had a Little Lamb across three genres, science fiction, Western, and action, while Mary herself keeps not looking before she leaps: a meteor, outlaws, a bubble monster.
rows.coping: Grandma and Grandpa supply the tool, genre, the style a story is in, and each swap brings its own gear: rocket suits, a ketchup shootout, a bubble emergency. The lesson underneath never changes, look before you leap, and the lights come back on mid-genre.
rows.notes: mixed age: the bubble monster plays 2-4; the same story told three ways, and what a genre actually changes, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'fun genre twists on a familiar favorite' omits the blackout frame, the three-genre run, and the repeated look-before-you-leap spine. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: A blackout cancels movie night, so Piper performs Mary Had a Little Lamb three times, as science fiction with rocket suits, as a Western with a ketchup-sheriff showdown, and as an action picture with a bubble monster. Each genre change swaps the setting and keeps the lesson: Mary, look before you leap. Lights, and story night, are restored by the final genre.

rows.episode_title: Mary Had a Little Chicken / The Princess, the Chicken, and the Pea
rows.segment_title: The Princess, the Chicken, and the Pea
rows.synopsis: Piper puts fun genre twists on a familiar favorite. When a royal athlete can't fall asleep, Piper hunts the cause.
rows.situation: Princess Emerald cannot sleep before her pole vault tournament, and every fix causes a new problem: a cat invited in, a dinner bell rung quietly, knights awake and hungry, a spooked horse, a windmill, a blanketless dragon. The kingdom is wide awake because Piper keeps solving one link at a time.
rows.coping: Papa teaches cause and effect, why something happens and what happened, then how to think backwards from the effect you want. One dragon fireball relights the lantern, the horse stops, the wind dies, the blanket returns, the knights get tomatoes, and the kingdom sleeps in one linked chain.
rows.notes: mixed age: the sleepy chain reaction plays 2-4; tracing an effect back to its cause, and fixing the first link instead of the last, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'a royal athlete can't fall asleep, Piper hunts the cause' omits the cascade of Piper-caused side effects and the backwards-thinking fix. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Princess Emerald needs sleep before the big tournament, and Piper's kind fixes keep causing new problems: cat, bell, knights, horse, windmill, dragon. Papa teaches cause and effect and how to think backwards from the effect you want, so one well-aimed fireball settles the whole kingdom. The princess sleeps, vaults, and wins, and a stick fort gets rebuilt by the same logic.

rows.episode_title: The Magnificent Magician of the Mailbox / Once Upon a Chicken
rows.segment_title: The Magnificent Magician of the Mailbox
rows.synopsis: Theodore, Duckston, and Piper work together on an illustrated story. Mrs. Slothworth teaches a lesson about collaboration.
rows.situation: Three writers want one driveway story about three different things, waffles, robots, magic, and the chalk is not moving. When they do collaborate, each wish-giver in the story turns out to already have the thing they were searching for, which they only notice by comparing notes.
rows.coping: Papa breaks collaboration into brainstorm, then choose together: a rain cloud, a robot, and a koala share one tub and one quest. When the magician has no snack, Duckston's waffle idea finally gets its moment, and the wishes are already granted by the journey itself.
rows.notes: mixed age: the purple brick path plays 2-4; brainstorming as a group skill where every idea waits for its turn, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'work together on an illustrated story' omits the brainstorm mechanics and the wishes-already-came-true twist. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Three driveway writers with three incompatible story ideas learn collaboration from Papa, brainstorm everything, then choose together, and a rain cloud, a robot, and a koala set off in a wheeled tub. When the Magician of the Mailbox cannot grant wishes on an empty stomach, the leftover waffle idea saves the day. The magician's real magic is the reveal: every wish already came true somewhere on the Purple Brick Path.

rows.episode_title: The Magnificent Magician of the Mailbox / Once Upon a Chicken
rows.synopsis: Theodore, Duckston, and Piper work together on an illustrated story. Mrs. Slothworth teaches a lesson about collaboration.
rows.situation: Cupcakes are passed out by label, writer gets the book, athlete gets the basketball, and Piper quietly takes the one she did not want. Two storybook princess tales in a row play out exactly as predicted, rescued princess, mean dragon, happily ever after, and the class calls every beat before it happens.
rows.coping: Piper rewrites the clichés: a princess who surfs, a sea monster best friend, a kind witch with a growing potion, knights who need rescuing and prefer sand waterslides. CJ's callback lands at snack time, and the cupcakes get re-dealt by desire.
rows.notes: mixed age: the surfing princess plays 2-4; noticing a pattern you were handed, and choosing your own version, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Mrs. Slothworth teaches a lesson about collaboration' belongs to the other story; tags anchor on segment_title plus the script. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Two princess stories in a row unfold exactly as predicted, and Mrs. Slothworth names the culprit: clichés, ideas so familiar you can guess the ending. Piper rewrites one until nothing can be called, a surfing princess, a sea monster bestie, a helpful witch, and the lesson leaks into snack time where the cupcakes are being assigned by stereotype. Piper gets the basketball cupcake she actually wanted.

rows.episode_title: The Royal Rollercoaster / Clucky Sinclair and the Three Bears
rows.synopsis: Piper and friends help the King build an exciting new ride. Hoping to solve a mystery, Piper and Clucky Sinclair make inferences.
rows.situation: The King's knights have never ridden a roller coaster, let alone built one, and Piper's own expertise turns out to be a ride on one, not blueprints. The carnival is tonight, and the royal thing to do is cancel it.
rows.coping: Piper learns research as a real skill with four doors: read about it, ask an expert, run an experiment, experience it yourself. Each door adds a piece, wood alone fails, Ms. Duck's design matters, the building set finds the right steepness, and the field trip finishes the lesson off-page.
rows.notes: mixed age: the carnival build plays 2-4; research as a thing writers do, with a design before a build, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'help the King build an exciting new ride' omits the four-methods-of-research structure and the field-trip coda. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The King wants a royal roller coaster by carnival time and his knights have never seen one up close; Piper's ride history does not survive contact with blueprints. Research becomes the hero: a book, an engineer on a video call, a design, and a building-set experiment that finds the right steepness. The carnival opens on a working coaster, and the class field trip is the truest research of all.

rows.episode_title: The Royal Rollercoaster / Clucky Sinclair and the Three Bears
rows.segment_title: Clucky Sinclair and the Three Bears
rows.synopsis: Piper and friends help the King build an exciting new ride. Hoping to solve a mystery, Piper and Clucky Sinclair make inferences.
rows.situation: Theodore's lunch box vanishes and a lunch-monster is the leading theory, while in the Three Bears' cottage, porridge disappears and the bears guess monsters too. Nobody is using the clues that are already on the floor.
rows.coping: Clucky Sinclair teaches inference, using clues to make a kind of guess: golden hair points to Goldilocks, muddy footprints and a two-handled basket point to the troll. The detective work comes home and finds the lunch box in the hallway, exactly where the last clue said.
rows.notes: mixed age: the bear-cottage mystery plays 2-4; a guess built from clues versus a wild guess, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Hoping to solve a mystery, Piper and Clucky Sinclair make inferences' omits the lunch-monster theory, the troll's side of the story, and the apology-and-mushroom-feast ending. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Theodore's lunch box is missing and the lunch-monster theory is winning, so story time supplies the tool: inferences, guesses built from clues. Clucky Sinclair walks the Three Bears through evidence, hair, footprints, a swapped basket, all the way to a truffling troll with a side of the story and an apology. The same method recovers the lunch box from the hallway, before lunch.

rows.episode_title: Wonder Chicken Returns / Professor Goose Visits
rows.synopsis: Grandma teaches a valuable lesson as Piper suits up for a superhero mission. A popular author visits Piper's school.
rows.situation: Wonder Chicken befriends her supervillain over ice cream, and the friendship becomes the problem: every game Von Duck and Mega Potato play splashes, freezes, or wrecks the city, and stopping them wrecks the friendship. Tag without a tag, an unspoken hurt, is humming underneath in the yard.
rows.coping: The Coop of Wisdom sorts three kinds of conflict, story, internal, and with the environment, and the resolution Piper writes is a feelings conversation: you are wrecking the city for everyone who lives here. The friends find a potato-sized compromise, and CJ finds her voice about tag.
rows.notes: mixed age: the belly-flop plot plays 2-4; naming what you feel and saying it to a friend, plus the harder truth that you can like someone and still need them to stop, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Grandma teaches a valuable lesson' omits the friendship-with-a-villain bind and the CJ tag subplot. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Wonder Chicken makes peace with Dr. Von Duck and discovers that friendships create their own conflicts: the games she loves wreck the city she protects. Wisdom Chicken helps her sort story, internal, and environmental conflict, and the fix is a sit-down talk where feelings get said out loud. CJ tries the same move at tag, and gets tagged at last.

rows.episode_title: Wonder Chicken Returns / Professor Goose Visits
rows.synopsis: Grandma teaches a valuable lesson as Piper suits up for a superhero mission. A popular author visits Piper's school.
rows.situation: Duckston's invention works beautifully and has a terrible name, Squishy Reading Chair with Page Flipper, and a real author needs invented words for a book due at the Musictorium. The flooflephone is crushed, a swamp is stickly, and a bird has no name.
rows.coping: The class co-writes with Professor Goose using imaginative language, brand-new words that make a reader smile: the upsie-downsie-sideways-enator, the double-roller-flipper-mobile, the flobble-horn. Naming things turns out to be half of making them, and Duckston's invention leaves as the squish-tastic read-o-matic.
rows.notes: mixed age: the made-up words play 2-4 purely as sound; co-creating with a real author, and naming as an act of imagination, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'A popular author visits' omits the broken flooflephone, the swamp crossing, and that the kids' words end up in the book. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Professor Goose visits Slothessori and the class becomes her co-writers, inventing words for a story that keeps breaking its own props: a crushed flooflephone becomes the flobble-horn, a swamp demands the double-roller-flipper-mobile. Duckston's anonymous invention gets named at last, the squish-tastic read-o-matic, because a good invention deserves a word that makes you smile.

rows.episode_title: Starting from Scratch / Snow White's Seven
rows.synopsis: Benjamin asks Piper to create an original story. Piper meets new friends while trying to understand a strange new land.
rows.situation: Piper promises Benjamin a brand-new story and meets her enemy, the blank page, twice, at the beginning and again in the middle. The stakes are a bedtime and a hungry alien picnic on the rings of Saturn.
rows.coping: Papa supplies the writer's toolkit in order: fold the paper into a book, know your audience, make a word web, then write the ending part last. A meteor shower and a picnic-stealing space monster turn out to be one story, and everyone at the picnic is a friend Piper wrote in.
rows.notes: mixed age: the space picnic plays 2-4; the blank page, and the tools for filling it one beat at a time, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Benjamin asks Piper to create an original story' omits the word web, the mid-story blank page, and the monster's picnic motive. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Benjamin wants a story that has never existed, and Piper discovers the blank page is the hardest part of writing. Papa hands her the tools one at a time, a folded book, an audience, a word web of space words, and Commander Chicken flies through meteors and a food-stealing monster to a picnic on Saturn's rings. The monster was only looking for something to bring, and the story ends with an immediate encore request.

rows.episode_title: Starting from Scratch / Snow White's Seven
rows.synopsis: Benjamin asks Piper to create an original story. Piper meets new friends while trying to understand a strange new land.
rows.situation: The quilt squares are blank because nobody knows what makes them theirs, and Piper's Snow White draft has seven friends who are exactly the same. A locked castle, a moat, a guard dragon, and a jumbo instruction manual stand between the King and his surprise.
rows.coping: Piper learns quirk, the thing that makes someone stand out, and hands each friend one, bouncy, stretchy, speed-reader, clumsy on purpose. The quilt squares fill with the same material, the things that make each kid special, and the castle opens.
rows.notes: mixed age: the sevenquirks rescue plays 2-4; everyone contributing the thing that makes them different, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Piper meets new friends while trying to understand a strange new land' is the other story; tags anchor on segment_title plus the script. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Seven identical friends are useless in a castle rescue, and seven blank quilt squares are just as stuck, until Piper learns the word quirk. Each friend contributes exactly their difference, bounce, stretch, speed-reading, well-aimed clumsiness, and each kid decorates a square with theirs. A dragon gets lulled by guitar, the King gets his surprise, and the quilts get finished.
